================================================================================
ДЖН1-LANGUAGE v6.63.932 — MASTER VOCABULARY EXPANSION
================================================================================

The goal of this edition is breadth plus native identity: a large English
headword inventory, then dedicated domain coverage, without returning to a
pure transliteration style.

MASTER RULES 102–126
M102. Every English headword has one canonical DXN1 dictionary key.
M103. Duplicate English headwords are prohibited in newly added entries.
M104. Different meanings of one English headword remain under one dictionary key.
M105. Synonyms remain separate English headwords but may share a documented root family.
M106. Native adaptation outranks literal transcription in Standard speech once registered.
M107. Literal forms remain allowed as transparent aliases for learning and precision.
M108. High-frequency words may become strongly irregular over time.
M109. A native irregular form is still required to obey the no-duplicate headword rule.
M110. Native forms may change vowels, consonants, syllable count, and endings.
M111. Native forms should follow existing ДЖН1 sound patterns rather than random changes.
M112. Medical terminology may be shorter in everyday speech and longer in formal writing.
M113. Plant names may favor open syllables and softer endings.
M114. Mineral names may favor crisp consonant clusters and compact forms.
M115. Animal names should remain clearly distinguishable in ordinary speech.
M116. Chemical and physical terminology may retain international aliases.
M117. Scientific aliases do not create duplicate English dictionary keys.
M118. A productive suffix is attached to the native root, never the English source.
M119. Gender -ью and -ьж remain post-root and post-derivation.
M120. Plural marking follows gender when both are present.
M121. -ер, -ник, -ист can form people/specialists.
M122. -ка can form tools/objects.
M123. -инг can form processes/activities.
M124. -ед can form completed states/results.
M125. -ный and -но form adjective/adverb families where useful.
M126. Future domain catalogs must continue from the current English inventory rather
     than re-adding existing headwords.

GRAMMAR & SENTENCE STRUCTURE
================================================================================
GR127. A clause normally contains one finite verb center unless it is coordinated.
GR128. Subject omission is allowed in Casual mode when the subject is obvious from context.
GR129. Standard mode restores an omitted subject when ambiguity could occur.
GR130. Hard mode may omit repeated subjects across adjacent coordinated clauses.
GR131. A subject pronoun cannot be repeated for emphasis unless the repetition is intentional.
GR132. Object pronouns normally follow the verb.
GR133. Two adjacent pronouns require a role particle or reordered structure when ambiguity occurs.
GR134. Adjectives normally precede the noun they describe.
GR135. Multiple adjectives preserve a readable modifier-to-noun order.
GR136. A strong/emphatic adjective may move closer to the noun.
GR137. Adverbs normally precede the verb phrase they modify.
GR138. Time adverbs may appear at clause start or end.
GR139. Place phrases normally follow the object.
GR140. Mood particles normally occupy the final position of the clause.
GR141. Question marker ли follows the questioned clause or focused element.
GR142. Question words do not require ли when their interrogative role is obvious.
GR143. Negative не remains closest to the verb it negates.
GR144. A sentence with multiple verbs may repeat tense/aspect markers per clause.
GR145. Coordinated verbs sharing one subject may omit a repeated subject.
GR146. Coordinated clauses may share a tense marker only when the time reference is identical.
GR147. Contrastive то marks the topic before the main clause when emphasis is desired.
GR148. Emphatic же normally appears immediately after the focused word or phrase.
GR149. Casual filler ка may be omitted without changing propositional meaning.
GR150. Softener ну normally appears at the beginning of a clause.
GR151. A direct command may omit its subject.
GR152. Commands can be softened by ну, ка, or a polite particle.
GR153. Strong commands may use repeated punctuation in Casual or Nightmare mode.
GR154. Exclamations do not change basic word order.
GR155. Conditional clauses use иф at the start of the condition.
GR156. Consequence clauses normally follow the condition unless marked for emphasis.
GR157. Because-clauses normally follow the main clause.
GR158. Relative clauses should place the defining information directly after the noun.
GR159. A repeated noun may be replaced by a pronoun inside a relative clause.
GR160. Embedded questions retain normal question-word order but may drop ли.
GR161. Reported speech may use сэй + clause without quotation marks in Casual mode.
GR162. Formal quoted speech preserves quotation marks.
GR163. A sentence may contain multiple discourse particles, but only one may carry primary emphasis.
GR164. Repetition of a complete clause indicates emotional insistence.
GR165. Repetition of only the final word indicates correction or reinforcement.
GR166. Parenthetical information is syntactically optional.
GR167. Parenthetical particles never control tense.
GR168. A standalone fragment is valid in Casual mode when conversational intent is clear.
GR169. Standard mode prefers complete clauses in instructional writing.
GR170. Hard mode allows safe deletion of recoverable function words.

TENSE, ASPECT & MODALITY
================================================================================
TM171. Present remains the unmarked default.
TM172. Past был precedes aspect when both are present.
TM173. Future буд precedes aspect when both are present.
TM174. Continuous из follows the tense marker.
TM175. Perfect/completed ду follows the tense marker.
TM176. Only one primary tense marker occurs per clause.
TM177. Only one primary aspect marker occurs per verb phrase.
TM178. Modal words may occur between tense/aspect particles and the lexical verb when needed.
TM179. Ability uses a modal root rather than a new verb conjugation class.
TM180. Obligation and permission use separate modal words.
TM181. A modal may scope over a coordinated verb phrase when both verbs share the same modality.
TM182. Negation precedes the modal when the intended meaning is 'must not/cannot'.
TM183. Negation after the modal may instead negate the action itself; ambiguity should be avoided.
TM184. Time words can clarify otherwise ambiguous tense.
TM185. A future time word does not automatically replace буд in formal Standard mode.
TM186. A past time word does not automatically replace был in formal Standard mode.
TM187. Casual speech may omit redundant tense markers when context is obvious.
TM188. Hard mode may compress repeated tense markers across a sequence.
TM189. A completed state may use ду without implying a specific past time.
TM190. Continuous из emphasizes duration, process, or temporary activity.
TM191. Aspect is semantic, not a person/number conjugation.
TM192. Modality can combine with tense but should not create stacked tense markers.
TM193. Conditional modality should be resolved at clause level rather than by a special verb ending.
TM194. Hearsay may be marked by a discourse particle instead of changing verb morphology.
TM195. Uncertainty may be marked lexically with maybe-like particles.
TM196. Strong certainty may use же or a dedicated certainty word.
TM197. Habitual actions may remain unmarked when general time is obvious.
TM198. Repeated actions may use a lexical frequency word rather than a new aspect marker.
TM199. Sequence of completed events is normally expressed with multiple clauses.
TM200. Aspect does not change the root form.

PRONOUNS, GENDER & AGREEMENT
================================================================================
PG201. Pronouns retain their core forms across tense.
PG202. Gender is optional unless the speaker needs to identify or emphasize gender.
PG203. The canonical feminine suffix is -ью.
PG204. The canonical masculine suffix is -ьж.
PG205. Gender suffixes attach after lexical and productive derivation.
PG206. Gender suffixes never attach to invariant particles.
PG207. Gender suffixes never attach to tense/aspect markers.
PG208. A gendered occupation can be formed from the native occupation root plus -ью or -ьж.
PG209. A gendered relationship noun can use the same suffix system.
PG210. Gender suffixes do not alter the core English semantic key.
PG211. A word with an already gendered lexical meaning may remain unmarked if context is clear.
PG212. Neutral/unspecified forms remain the default when gender is irrelevant.
PG213. The old prefix-style gender forms are retained as emphatic/legacy forms where already defined.
PG214. New standard entries should prefer the canonical suffix system.
PG215. A word should not carry both a legacy gender prefix and a canonical gender suffix in Standard mode.
PG216. Hard mode may use legacy markers for stylistic emphasis if meaning remains clear.
PG217. Plural forms follow the gender suffix when both markers are needed.
PG218. Collective groups can remain unmarked when mixed or unspecified.
PG219. A gender suffix never changes tense/aspect.
PG220. Possessives can be gendered only when the intended referent requires it.
PG221. Gender marking on objects is disfavored unless the object has a personified meaning.
PG222. Personified objects may be gendered in creative writing.
PG223. Proper names keep their natural identity and are not automatically gender-suffixed.
PG224. Occupational gender marking is optional in Casual mode.
PG225. Standard mode uses gender marking when it prevents ambiguity.

WORD FORMATION & ENDINGS
================================================================================
WF226. The canonical order is prefix + root + derivation + gender + plural.
WF227. A tense/aspect particle stays outside the lexical word.
WF228. Derivational suffixes cannot precede the root.
WF229. Gender suffixes cannot appear before the root.
WF230. Two incompatible derivational families should not be stacked.
WF231. A second derivational suffix is allowed when the first creates the correct semantic base.
WF232. -ер forms an agent/person who performs or specializes in the root action.
WF233. -ник forms an associated person, holder, or role.
WF234. -ист forms a specialist, practitioner, or adherent.
WF235. -инг forms an activity, process, or ongoing phenomenon.
WF236. -ед forms a completed result or resulting state.
WF237. -ка forms a concrete tool, object, or implement.
WF238. -зона forms an area, field, or environment.
WF239. -макс marks deliberately extreme or maximal intensity.
WF240. -мод marks a mode or state of operation.
WF241. -вэйв marks a style, trend, aesthetic, or movement.
WF242. -синк marks alignment or synchronization.
WF243. -дроп marks a release, drop, or sudden appearance.
WF244. -лооп marks repetition or cycling.
WF245. -стрим marks continuous flow or broadcasting.
WF246. -крафт marks making, building, or crafted output.
WF247. -глоу marks visible aura, shine, or enhanced presence.
WF248. -пак marks a bundle or grouped collection.
WF249. -ность creates an abstract quality or property.
WF250. -ство creates an abstract state, system, or collective concept.
WF251. -ный creates an adjective from a native root where natural.
WF252. -но creates an adverbial form where natural.
WF253. -ью creates feminine person/gender marking.
WF254. -ьж creates masculine person/gender marking.
WF255. A derivation should preserve the semantic center of its root.
WF256. If a derivation produces an accidental duplicate, reshape the derived form.
WF257. Native irregular roots take precedence over literal roots for new derivations.
WF258. Hyphenated multiple-prefix constructions are treated as compounds.
WF259. A compound may lexicalize into a frozen word if frequent.
WF260. Frozen compounds should not automatically accept every productive suffix.
WF261. If a compound needs further morphology, create an explicit derived form.
WF262. New roots should be tested with at least one noun-like or verb-like use.
WF263. New roots should have a stable English semantic key.
WF264. A native twist should never create an accidental second English headword.
WF265. Productive morphology is preferred over inventing arbitrary synonyms.
WF266. Irregular words are reserved for frequent, culturally important, or especially natural forms.
WF267. A new irregular form should be documented in the rulebook.
WF268. Suffix pronunciation may smooth to avoid awkward consonant clusters.
WF269. A final vowel may be inserted before a suffix when readability requires it.
WF270. A final vowel may disappear before a suffix when the resulting form is easier to pronounce.
WF271. Repeated suffixes are normally prohibited unless they create a documented semantic contrast.
WF272. Prefix and suffix meanings must remain compositional unless a word is marked irregular.
WF273. Technical roots may use international morphology when precision outweighs native styling.
WF274. Everyday roots should prefer native styling over strict international morphology.
WF275. A word's class should be recoverable from context even if morphology is irregular.

PRONUNCIATION & ORTHOGRAPHY
================================================================================
OR276. Cyrillic is the default native writing system.
OR277. Latin is retained for names, URLs, code, brands, identifiers, and deliberate emphasis.
OR278. ДЖН1 is the canonical native rendering of DXN1.
OR279. X is rendered as Ж in the native name rather than using a nonexistent Cyrillic X equivalent.
OR280. The digit 1 remains unchanged in ДЖН1.
OR281. Native forms may contain mixed script only for clearly marked technical or stylistic reasons.
OR282. A native word should be pronounceable directly from its Cyrillic form.
OR283. Hard-mode vowel deletion never removes gender markers.
OR284. Hard-mode vowel deletion never removes tense/aspect particles.
OR285. Casual repetition of vowels can express emotion.
OR286. Repeated consonants can express stress or impact but should be used sparingly in Standard mode.
OR287. Capitalization follows ordinary sentence capitalization unless a stylistic mode overrides it.
OR288. Acronyms may remain uppercase.
OR289. Proper names preserve original capitalization when written in Latin.
OR290. Native-translated proper names may use title capitalization.
OR291. Apostrophes are optional in foreign names but discouraged inside core DXN1 roots.
OR292. Hyphens mark deliberate multi-root compounds or stacked technical prefixes.
OR293. Spaces separate ordinary lexical words.
OR294. A fused compound requires a dictionary entry if it is treated as one lexical item.
OR295. Punctuation does not normally alter grammatical word order.
OR296. Commas may mark direct address.
OR297. Em dashes can mark interruption, contrast, or dramatic pause.
OR298. Ellipses may mark hesitation, trailing speech, or omission.
OR299. Question marks may be doubled for strong disbelief in Casual/Nightmare mode.
OR300. Exclamation marks may be repeated for intensity in Casual/Nightmare mode.
OR301. Standard prose should avoid excessive punctuation stacking.
OR302. Emoji are treated as discourse cues, not grammatical words.
OR303. Repeated letters are orthographic emotion markers, not new dictionary entries.
OR304. A Hard-mode compressed word remains linked to its Standard canonical root.
OR305. Nightmare spelling may be visually extreme but must remain decodable by expert speakers.

MODE SYSTEM
================================================================================
MO306. Casual prioritizes speed and social readability.
MO307. Standard prioritizes dictionary consistency and clarity.
MO308. Hard prioritizes compression and coded visual texture.
MO309. Nightmare prioritizes maximum compression while retaining expert parseability.
MO310. Casual may use frozen contractions.
MO311. Standard avoids frozen contractions in instructional text.
MO312. Hard may omit recoverable particles.
MO313. Nightmare may fuse particles with neighboring words when documented.
MO314. A speaker may shift modes mid-conversation.
MO315. A mode shift should not silently change the underlying meaning.
MO316. A formal technical document should default to Standard.
MO317. Gaming chat may default to Casual or Hard.
MO318. Secret-note writing may use Hard or Nightmare.
MO319. Creative poetry may intentionally violate normal mode restrictions.
MO320. A poetic violation is not automatically a new grammatical rule.
MO321. Mode is a surface style layer over the same core grammar.
MO322. Canonical dictionary forms remain Standard even when a Hard form is more common in chat.
MO323. Every Hard/Nightmare form must be traceable back to a canonical root.
MO324. Mode compression may not erase distinctions that would make the sentence ambiguous.
MO325. A speaker may deliberately restore vowels to clarify a compressed word.

SEMANTICS & AMBIGUITY
================================================================================
SA326. Context resolves ordinary polysemy unless two readings remain equally likely.
SA327. When ambiguity matters, use a clarifying modifier instead of inventing a new root.
SA328. A duplicate DXN1 surface form for different English meanings should be avoided.
SA329. If a collision is unavoidable, the less frequent form receives a semantic twist.
SA330. Technical contexts may prioritize domain-specific meaning over everyday meaning.
SA331. Idioms may override literal meanings when marked as idioms.
SA332. Slang meanings should be marked separately from Standard meanings.
SA333. Figurative meanings do not require a new root when the metaphor is transparent.
SA334. A word can carry multiple numbered senses under the same English headword.
SA335. Sense order should place the most common meaning first.
SA336. Rare senses may be labeled specialist, archaic, slang, or regional.
SA337. New specialist vocabulary should never overwrite an established everyday sense.
SA338. A domain label is semantic metadata, not a grammatical marker.
SA339. Person, object, action, state, and place meanings should be distinguished when needed.
SA340. A root may shift word class through productive derivation.
SA341. Metaphorical compounds follow normal compound order.
SA342. Hyperbole is stylistic and does not create a new literal meaning.
SA343. Irony may be marked with context, punctuation, or a discourse particle.
SA344. A speaker can explicitly disambiguate with же, то, or a clarifying noun phrase.
SA345. Dictionary examples should demonstrate the common reading before rare readings.

NUMBERS, MEASURES & TIME
================================================================================
NU346. Numbers remain independent lexical roots rather than inflected noun forms.
NU347. Compound numbers follow the established English-like composition order.
NU348. Ordinals are derived from the cardinal root by the dedicated ordinal pattern.
NU349. Negative values use a negative marker before the number.
NU350. Fractions use numerator + fraction marker + denominator.
NU351. Percentages place the number before the percent word.
NU352. Decimal numbers preserve the decimal separator in writing.
NU353. Measurements place the quantity before the unit.
NU354. Unit names remain invariant after numerals unless a special lexical form exists.
NU355. Clock time may use both numeric and spoken forms.
NU356. Dates use an unambiguous day/month/year ordering in formal writing.
NU357. Relative time words may override an otherwise vague tense interpretation.
NU358. Duration can be expressed numerically or with a time-unit noun.
NU359. Approximation uses dedicated approximate words rather than changing number morphology.
NU360. Range expressions use a consistent connector between the lower and upper values.

================================================================================

DS368. Gamer terminology may use international roots with native endings.

DS374. Meme forms are considered temporary slang until lexicalized.
DS375. Irony markers do not alter tense.
DS376. Sarcasm relies primarily on context and particle choice.
DS377. Social titles can be native roots or international names.
DS378. Respectful address may use titles rather than pronouns.
DS379. Insults can be compounded, but compound meaning remains compositional unless lexicalized.
DS380. Positive intensifiers and negative intensifiers should remain semantically distinct.

control the living, native behavior of ДЖН1 rather than one isolated vocabulary
batch.

ТВА РУЛЕС 001 — One English headword has one canonical dictionary identity.

ТВА РУЛЕС 016 — A domain label never creates a second English key.

ТВА РУЛЕС 022 — A legacy form can be preserved without remaining the preferred form.

ТВА РУЛЕС 024 — A historical form must be labeled historical rather than silently treated as current.

ТВА РУЛЕС 140 — Titles can be gender-marked when the role is the focus.

SYNTAX / CLAUSE FLOW

ТВА РУЛЕС 141 — Default sentence order remains subject + tense/aspect + verb + object + place + mood.
ТВА РУЛЕС 142 — A place phrase normally follows the object unless focused.
ТВА РУЛЕС 143 — A time phrase may open or close the clause.
ТВА РУЛЕС 144 — A mood particle normally ends the clause.
ТВА РУЛЕС 145 — же follows the focused element whenever practical.
ТВА РУЛЕС 146 — то marks topic or contrast rather than ordinary emphasis.
ТВА РУЛЕС 147 — ну normally softens or delays the beginning of a clause.
ТВА РУЛЕС 148 — ка colors casual tone without adding new propositional meaning.
ТВА РУЛЕС 149 — не stays close to the word it negates.
ТВА РУЛЕС 150 — ли marks a yes/no question when needed.
ТВА РУЛЕС 151 — Question words normally remove the need for ли.
ТВА РУЛЕС 152 — A command may omit the subject.
ТВА РУЛЕС 153 — A polite command may add a softener.
ТВА РУЛЕС 154 — A strong command may use punctuation for intensity instead of new morphology.
ТВА РУЛЕС 155 — A conditional begins with иф unless another discourse structure explicitly marks the condition.
ТВА РУЛЕС 156 — A because-clause normally follows its main clause.
ТВА РУЛЕС 157 — A sequence of events normally uses separate clause heads.
ТВА РУЛЕС 158 — A relative clause should sit close to the noun it defines.
ТВА РУЛЕС 159 — Repeated subjects may be omitted in Casual mode when obvious.
ТВА РУЛЕС 160 — Standard mode restores omitted subjects when ambiguity is likely.

ROLE / CASE PARTICLES

ТВА РУЛЕС 161 — Subject role is normally unmarked.
ТВА РУЛЕС 162 — Object marking is used only when word order cannot safely disambiguate.
ТВА РУЛЕС 163 — Recipient role uses фор where the existing system requires it.
ТВА РУЛЕС 164 — Instrument role uses виз where the existing system requires it.
ТВА РУЛЕС 165 — Location uses ин, ат, or он according to containment and surface logic.
ТВА РУЛЕС 166 — Role particles do not take gender suffixes.
ТВА РУЛЕС 167 — Role particles do not take plural suffixes.
ТВА РУЛЕС 168 — Role particles do not take productive lexical suffixes.
ТВА РУЛЕС 169 — Pronoun objects that already encode role do not need redundant object marking.
ТВА РУЛЕС 170 — If two role markers create a collision, word order wins and redundant marking is removed.

TENSE / ASPECT

ТВА РУЛЕС 171 — Present is the zero-marked tense.
ТВА РУЛЕС 172 — был marks past.
ТВА РУЛЕС 173 — буд marks future.
ТВА РУЛЕС 174 — из marks ongoing/continuous aspect.
ТВА РУЛЕС 175 — ду marks completed/perfect aspect.
ТВА РУЛЕС 176 — Tense precedes aspect.
ТВА РУЛЕС 177 — One primary tense marker per clause.
ТВА РУЛЕС 178 — One primary aspect marker per verb phrase.
ТВА РУЛЕС 179 — A time adverb may clarify tense without becoming a tense marker.
ТВА РУЛЕС 180 — A redundant tense marker may be dropped in Casual speech when the time is obvious.

MODE / REGISTER

ТВА РУЛЕС 181 — Casual prioritizes speed.
ТВА РУЛЕС 182 — Standard prioritizes clarity and canonical forms.
ТВА РУЛЕС 183 — Hard prioritizes compression and coded texture.
ТВА РУЛЕС 184 — Nightmare prioritizes extreme compression but remains expert-decodable.
ТВА РУЛЕС 185 — A Standard word is always the reference form for learning.
ТВА РУЛЕС 186 — A Hard form must map back to a Standard form.
ТВА РУЛЕС 187 — A Nightmare form must map back to a Hard and Standard form.
ТВА РУЛЕС 188 — Casual slang can be frozen without becoming productive grammar.
ТВА РУЛЕС 189 — Formal writing should avoid temporary meme forms.
ТВА РУЛЕС 190 — Game chat may favor Hard vocabulary without changing core grammar.

SLANG / SOCIAL LANGUAGE

ТВА РУЛЕС 191 — Slang can shorten frequent roots.
ТВА РУЛЕС 192 — Slang may create affectionate diminutives with -ик when natural.
ТВА РУЛЕС 193 — Slang may create exaggerated forms with -ища.
ТВА РУЛЕС 194 — Slang may freeze compounds that would be unusual in Standard.
ТВА РУЛЕС 195 — Internet abbreviations can remain invariant.
ТВА РУЛЕС 196 — Meme words remain temporary until adopted into the lexicon.
ТВА РУЛЕС 197 — Gamer terms can use native suffixes.
ТВА РУЛЕС 198 — Trash-talk vocabulary should describe behavior, attitude, skill, or energy rather than protected traits.
ТВА РУЛЕС 199 — Profanity intensity should be treated as register, not grammar.
ТВА РУЛЕС 200 — A profanity root may serve as an intensifier only when that use is documented.

SCIENCE / MEDICINE / NATURE

ТВА РУЛЕС 201 — Specialist words may keep international scientific roots.
ТВА РУЛЕС 202 — Everyday medical words prefer shorter native forms.
ТВА РУЛЕС 203 — Formal medical writing may prefer transparent international terminology.
ТВА РУЛЕС 204 — Disease families should reuse consistent native patterns.
ТВА РУЛЕС 205 — Anatomy terms should remain distinguishable in rapid speech.
ТВА РУЛЕС 206 — Plant names should favor stable root shapes so related species remain learnable.
ТВА РУЛЕС 207 — Minerals may use compact consonant patterns for easy differentiation.
ТВА РУЛЕС 208 — Animal names should avoid collision with common human names where possible.
ТВА РУЛЕС 209 — Scientific aliases do not create additional English headwords.
ТВА РУЛЕС 210 — Domain tags belong to dictionary metadata, not inside the word itself.

NUMBERS / MEASURES

ТВА РУЛЕС 211 — Numbers remain lexical roots.
ТВА РУЛЕС 212 — Compound numbers follow one stable composition order.
ТВА РУЛЕС 213 — Units follow numbers.
ТВА РУЛЕС 214 — Unit names remain invariant after numeric values unless a lexical exception is documented.
ТВА РУЛЕС 215 — Fractions use a stable numerator + fraction marker + denominator pattern.
ТВА РУЛЕС 216 — Negative numbers use a negative marker before the number.
ТВА РУЛЕС 217 — Ranges use one consistent range connector.
ТВА РУЛЕС 218 — Approximation is marked lexically rather than by changing the numeral.
ТВА РУЛЕС 219 — Dates should be written unambiguously in formal Standard mode.
ТВА РУЛЕС 220 — Time expressions may appear at the beginning of a clause for emphasis.

NAMES / PLACES / CULTURE

ТВА РУЛЕС 221 — Personal names remain identifiers unless lexicalized.
ТВА РУЛЕС 222 — Place names may be naturalized for local ДЖН1 use.
ТВА РУЛЕС 223 — Naturalized place names may keep a transparent international alias.
ТВА РУЛЕС 224 — Brand names remain Latin when branding is the important identity.
ТВА РУЛЕС 225 — A brand-derived common noun may receive a native lexical form.
ТВА РУЛЕС 226 — Fictional names can follow native ДЖН1 phonotactics.
ТВА РУЛЕС 227 — Factions can use compounds and productive endings.
ТВА РУЛЕС 228 — Titles may be translated while proper names remain unchanged.
ТВА РУЛЕС 229 — Historical names may retain a culturally established spelling.
ТВА РУЛЕС 230 — A place-name compound can become a lexicalized root when widely used.

WORDBOOK FORMAT

ТВА РУЛЕС 231 — Every canonical wordbook entry should show English headword, canonical ДЖН1 form, and meaning.
ТВА РУЛЕС 232 — Variants may appear after the canonical form.
ТВА РУЛЕС 233 — Casual forms should be labeled Casual.
ТВА РУЛЕС 234 — Hard forms should be labeled Hard.
ТВА РУЛЕС 235 — Legacy forms should be labeled Legacy rather than silently mixed with Canonical.
ТВА РУЛЕС 236 — Irregular forms should be labeled Irregular.
ТВА РУЛЕС 237 — Specialist entries should carry domain metadata.
ТВА РУЛЕС 238 — Proper names should carry Name metadata.
ТВА РУЛЕС 239 — Abbreviations should carry Abbreviation metadata.
ТВА РУЛЕС 240 — A headword should not appear twice merely because its metadata differs.

REVISION / VERSIONING

ТВА РУЛЕС 241 — A lexical-only release increments the final version component.
ТВА РУЛЕС 242 — A grammar restructuring may increment the middle component.
ТВА РУЛЕС 243 — A core identity change would increment the first component.
ТВА РУЛЕС 244 — The native name ДЖН1 does not change between minor lexical releases.
ТВА РУЛЕС 245 — Historical material remains readable after a version bump.
ТВА РУЛЕС 246 — New canonical forms should state what they replace when a legacy form exists.
ТВА РУЛЕС 247 — New rules should not silently contradict a still-active core rule.
ТВА РУЛЕС 248 — When a new rule refines an old rule, the new rule should state the scope of the refinement.
ТВА РУЛЕС 249 — A stylistic rule does not override grammar unless explicitly declared grammar-level.
ТВА РУЛЕС 250 — A slang rule does not override Standard morphology unless explicitly promoted.

QUALITY / ACCEPTANCE

ТВА РУЛЕС 251 — A new root must have one stable English semantic key.
ТВА РУЛЕС 252 — A new root must fit the native sound style or be marked Irregular.
ТВА РУЛЕС 253 — A new root should survive at least one Standard sentence test.
ТВА РУЛЕС 254 — A derived word should survive at least one morphology test.
ТВА РУЛЕС 255 — A gendered people-word should survive both -ью and -ьж tests when applicable.
ТВА РУЛЕС 256 — A technical word should survive a transparent-form comparison.
ТВА РУЛЕС 257 — A slang word should survive a register comparison.
ТВА РУЛЕС 258 — A Hard form should survive a reverse-reading test back to Standard.
ТВА РУЛЕС 259 — A new compound should pass a semantic-composition test.
ТВА РУЛЕС 260 — A new word that creates unacceptable ambiguity should be reshaped before promotion.

FINAL TWA PRINCIPLES

ТВА РУЛЕС 261 — Meaning first, native form second, style third.
ТВА РУЛЕС 262 — Canonical root first, derivation second, gender third, plural last.
ТВА РУЛЕС 263 — Standard is the reference; Casual, Hard, and Nightmare are surface modes.
ТВА РУЛЕС 264 — Native twists are intentional, documented, and learnable.
ТВА РУЛЕС 265 — Legacy forms remain history, not silent duplicates.
ТВА РУЛЕС 266 — Proper names stay names unless the language adopts them lexically.
ТВА РУЛЕС 267 — Specialist vocabulary may be transparent without becoming aesthetically alien.
ТВА РУЛЕС 268 — A duplicate is a governance failure, not a new word.
ТВА РУЛЕС 269 — A collision in ДЖН1 should be repaired before a new canonical form is published.
ТВА РУЛЕС 270 — ДЖН1 is allowed to evolve, but every evolution must remain traceable.

================================================================================
MANUAL REVIEW NOTE — v6.63.934
================================================================================
The previous edition contains multiple historical vocabulary layers and multiple
entry formats. During review, repeated lexical families and mixed dictionary
formats were observed. Therefore this edition does NOT claim that a programmatic
count alone proves the absence of duplicates. The governing standard is now the
ТВА РУЛЕС system above: one English headword = one canonical dictionary identity,
with variants, legacy forms, proper names, and specialist metadata kept as
secondary information rather than duplicate canonical entries.

The older vocabulary is intentionally preserved for continuity. Future canonical
cleanup should merge redundant entries without deleting their semantic history.

Version: ДЖН1-Language v6.63.934
Native name: ДЖН1-Language
Latin technical name: DXN1-Language
Creator: Dani Postma

================================================================================
ДЖН1-LANGUAGE v6.63.935 — CANONICAL WORDBOOK PATCH
================================================================================

This is a patch to v6.63.934, not a rebuilt/reordered replacement.

CANONICAL WORD RULES — ТВА РУЛЕС
ТВА1. One normalized English headword may appear only once as a canonical dictionary entry.
ТВА2. Case differences do not create separate English headwords.
ТВА3. Earlier duplicate entries are removed in favor of the newest retained entry.
ТВА4. Legacy duplicate lines are not kept as second dictionary entries.
ТВА5. A word's existing newest/adapted form is preferred over an older literal form.
ТВА6. Plurals, derived forms, and genuinely different English headwords remain separate only when they are themselves distinct English lexical entries.
ТВА7. Variant spellings may be documented in prose, but do not become duplicate canonical entries.
ТВА8. Proper names and identifiers remain non-canonical metadata unless deliberately defined as ordinary vocabulary.
ТВА9. Mixed dictionary formats are normalized by headword identity for duplicate checking.
ТВА10. Future patches must preserve the one-headword/one-canonical-entry rule.
ТВА11. Native forms such as -ью and -ьж remain part of the canonical morphology and are not treated as duplicate English words.
ТВА12. Historical/version notes belong in the rulebook, not as repeated dictionary entries.

All rules in this new layer use the identifier Ш + number and include concrete
lexical examples. The goal is to make the rulebook teach the language through
actual words rather than abstract statements.

Ш821. Every new dictionary rule should include at least one concrete lexical example; word: лэнго = language.
Ш822. A rule with no lexical example is considered incomplete in the teaching wordbook.
Ш823. Example words must use canonical Standard forms; word: хома = home.
Ш824. Gender examples must show the root before -ью/-ьж; word: тича = teacher → тичаью / тичаьж.
Ш825. Derived examples must show the native root before the productive ending; word: компа = computer → компа-ка.
Ш826. A rule can cite an everyday word and a specialist word together; words: фамо = family, медика = medicine.
Ш827. A rule may use a compound example; words: эрда = earth, вата = water → эрда-вата.
Ш828. Legacy material is never needed to explain a new rule; new rules use current canonical words only.
Ш829. The wordbook should prefer a small number of highly reusable rules over hundreds of exceptions.
Ш830. Every new rule must be compatible with the canonical headword policy.
